hypothesis.statement: Selecting the lowest realized-volatility quintile (K=20) of US87 equities with equal 5% weighting dampens drawdown in market pullbacks while maintaining a cash reserve for unlisted/short-history assets.
hypothesis.economic_rationale: Low-volatility anomaly in technology equities: extreme high-beta names suffer severe drawdowns and volatility drag during macro corrections, whereas steady cash-flow/low-beta tech names preserve capital.
hypothesis.expected_edge: Substantially lower maximum drawdown (-17.7% vs -28.0% for EW pool), positive risk-adjusted returns during tech shakeouts (+7.6% 1M when pool drops -11.1%).
falsification_criteria: Maximum drawdown exceeding that of the US87 Equal-Weight Pool Index (-28.0%).
Trailing 12-month excess return vs US87 EW pool dropping below -30% (unacceptable beta drag).
Cash drag ratio exceeding 30% of total portfolio value over 3 consecutive rebalances.

counter_evidence.observation: Lagged US87 Equal-Weight Pool Index by -20.4% during tech rally, confirming expected trade-off where defensive allocation underperforms during speculative bull runs.
Monthly turnover in volatile regime exceeded 40% as realized volatility quintile shifted rapidly, inducing 8 bps fee drag.

conclusion.verdict: Hypothesis supported in downside protection, challenged by persistent bull-market beta drag
conclusion.summary: Defensive thesis is verified: Max drawdown is -17.7% vs -28.0% for the pool. In 1M downturn, strategy gained +7.6% while pool dropped -11.1%. However, 1Y return trails the pool by -20.4% due to beta drag. It functions as an effective capital preservation sleeve rather than high-alpha driver.
supported_points: Downside protection verified: -17.7% MaxDD vs -28.0% pool MaxDD
Recent 1M market downturn: +7.6% vs -11.1% pool return
100% deterministic replay with valid Q-ledger hash chain
unresolved_risks: Severe beta lag during high-momentum market expansions
Realized volatility metric sensitivity to 20-session rolling window length
